entry.title: Any Tips to Speed Up Rendering Time?
entry.content:
Hey everyone,

I’ve been diving deep into video editing recently—mostly for YouTube and a few freelance projects—and I’ve hit a major bottleneck: rendering time. Even short videos in 1080p or 4K are taking an unusually long time to export, sometimes 30–45 minutes depending on the effects, transitions, and grading involved.

I’m currently editing with [insert your editor—e.g., Adobe Premiere Pro or DaVinci Resolve] on a decent mid-range setup (16 GB RAM, Ryzen 5, GTX 1660), but I feel like the software isn’t using my system efficiently. Before I look at hardware upgrades, I wanted to check in here for some practical advice.

Here are a few questions I have:

  • Are there render settings or formats I can tweak to speed up the process without heavily sacrificing quality?

  • I’ve heard of proxy editing—does it affect final render time or just smooth the workflow during editing?

  • How important is hardware acceleration, and how do I enable it correctly for my setup?

  • Are there better codecs or formats for faster rendering, especially for platforms like YouTube?

  • Would a dedicated rendering plugin help?

  • Should I be closing all background apps while exporting?

Also, I’ve seen some newer tools developed by video editing app development companies that claim faster rendering using AI or GPU optimization. Has anyone tried one of these newer editors or apps?

I’d appreciate any advice—even a few saved minutes per project would mean a lot over time. Thanks in advance, and looking forward to your tips!

entry.title: Best Practice für Automatic Implementation of SAP Notes (Transportreigabe)
entry.content:
Beim Update (SUM) wird die Option "Shadow System Development User" im Step "Required Shadow Parameters (PREP_INSTALL/SUBMOD_PREP_INSTALL/INITSHD) per Haken "Yes, SUM shall create a shadow system development user" verwendet.

Bei dem Vorgang wird auch die Funktion "Automated Reset of Obsolete SAP Notes" durchgeführt und auf einen Transport geschrieben. -> https://help.sap.com/docs/SLTOOLSET/b0d775c8a9fd47b985a5e66ddba31d33/46ebfbd34e3c46918ab73cc6919971f2.html#automated-reset-of-obsolete-sap-notes

Laut https://me.sap.com/notes/0003727019 schlägt die SAP vor, den TR nach dem Update freizugeben. Weiterhin wird von einem Transport ins Folgesystem abgeraten, sondern man solle dort erneut die gleiche Option (Yes, SUM shall create a shadow system development user) wie im Vorsystem ausführen .

Beim aktuellen Updateprozess lief der SPAU in eine Sperrsituation, weil Objekte auf dem besagten Transport standen. Da dies nur obsolete Hinweise betrifft, ist dies nicht kritisch.

Aber so stellt sich nun die Frage, wann genau der richtige Zeitpunkt für die Freigabe des Transports ist. Wie oben beschrieben, sollte das nach dem Update passieren. Unserer Meinung nach, wäre der richtige Zeitpunkt, vor SPAU.

Wann ist der tatsächlich richtige Zeitpunkt für die Freigabe des Transports?

Context
As part of an SAP migration (target system: NEW DEV, classicCTS/TMS landscape via STMS, not SAP Cloud Transport
Management),

we compared the list of transport requests (TRs) between the old system (OLD DEV) and the new one (NEW DEV).
Raw comparison result: - OLD DEV: 820 main transport requests, 598 tasks - NEW DEV: 536 common main transport requests identified -
877 references flagged as “missing” from NEW (552 of which are tasks whose parent TR is present, and 284 main TRs genuinely
absent) - Naive overall coverage: 38.2% — but actual coverage on
main TR
Problem
Before launching a mass import of the 284 missing main TRs, we want to avoid: - unnecessary re-imports of TRs that were already imported (but missing from the visible history or the compared export), -
dependency conflicts.

Our question to the community
What are the official recommended conditions and procedures for qualifying and then adding missing main transport requests
to the import queue in a classic CTS/TMS mass import, while avoiding unnecessary re-imports or a rollback  and is
there a standard SAP method to distinguish a genuinely “missing” TR from one that was already imported but is absent
from the visible history (case of a refresh/system copy)?
